searchText: good point, I don't think it's too bad to change them now How is everyone feeling about the name `process_execution_payload()` being re-purposed as a standalone function outside of block processing function? I think the new `process_execution_payload` in gloas should be named `process_execution_payload_envelope` to avoid namespace conflict + extra clarity in our codebase a minor PR here: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4772 we mention that validators don't have to broadcast blob sidecars since it is the responsibility of the builder. but if a validator self-builds, they still have to broadcast the sidecars by themselves. the validator would be the builder. I felt like it was worth clearing that? I like the current naming since it aligns with the gossip topic `execution_payload` 😂 https://x.com/potuz_eth/status/1995646043023966722?s=19 so if i m right, `bid.execution_payment` is only set for off-protocol payments purpose and there is no use of it in consensus? i m thinking of what would happen if `bid.value` and `bid.execution_payment` both are set to some value. if a builder sends a `SignedExecutionPayloadBid` to a proposer via a HTTP connection, they can set both values. There should ideally be no impact to doing this. the builder would end paying `bid.value` in the trustless way and the `bid.execution_payment` off-protocol(although there is no way to enforce this in protocol) correct, the builder can use this mechanism to signal an extra payment off-protocol if so they desire

excerpts.author: stefanbratanov
excerpts.content: good point, I don't think it's too bad to change them now

excerpts.author: nc1234
excerpts.content: How is everyone feeling about the name `process_execution_payload()` being re-purposed as a standalone function outside of block processing function? I think the new `process_execution_payload` in gloas should be named `process_execution_payload_envelope` to avoid namespace conflict + extra clarity in our codebase

excerpts.author: bharath.vedartham
excerpts.content:
a minor PR here: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4772 
we mention that validators don't have to broadcast blob sidecars since it is the responsibility of the builder. but if a validator self-builds, they still have to broadcast the sidecars by themselves. the validator would be the builder. 
I felt like it was worth clearing that?

excerpts.author: stefanbratanov
excerpts.content: I like the current naming since it aligns with the gossip topic `execution_payload`

excerpts.author: bharath.vedartham
excerpts.content:
so if i m right, `bid.execution_payment` is only set for off-protocol payments purpose and there is no use of it in consensus? i m thinking of what would happen if `bid.value` and `bid.execution_payment` both are set to some value. if a builder sends a `SignedExecutionPayloadBid` to a proposer via a HTTP connection, they can set both values.
There should ideally be no impact to doing this. the builder would end paying `bid.value` in the trustless way and the `bid.execution_payment` off-protocol(although there is no way to enforce this in protocol)

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: correct, the builder can use this mechanism to signal an extra payment off-protocol if so they desire
